parentQA.q: Is any of this allowed for a high school athlete?
parentQA.a: What we can do depends on your state. High school NIL rules vary by state and by athletic association, and some states allow nothing. Where it is not allowed, our role is to educate and advise your family at no cost, with no agreement, so you are ready when the rules change or when he enrolls. [Ryan: confirm the rules for this family's state and the schools in play before this goes out.]

Nothing. There is no fee for guidance during recruiting, and no agreement to sign until there is income it applies to, in a state where that is permitted. We walk through anything with a number on it in person.

Not if we are involved. Everything we do with a high school athlete is designed around keeping him eligible: we check the rules first, and we say no to things that put that at risk. We would rather lose a deal than cost him a season.

parentQA.q: How do we know which offers are real?
parentQA.a: We read them with you. A committable offer, a camp offer, a number in a press release and a scholarship are different things. We tell your family which one you are looking at.
